description:
Download v0.82.0 Here

Solsector adds Sol and many of its planets, minor planets, moons, and minor-planet moons in the top-right corner of the sector map. Each orbit is set to one of: real 2025 ephemerides, long-term orbital averages, or – for a few bodies – a plausible far-future configuration.

Sol is intended as a more difficult, but more rewarding, colonization experience, once you can beat the remnants. Over 50 conditions have been added; most are bad, but most are improvable. Your highs will be higher, and your lows will be much lower.

Dodge the hordes of [REDACTED] so large and numerous that they make a [THREAT: HIGH] system look like a surveying expedition. Or, snipe the nexuses and loot the system for its hordes of ruins. Or, jump in at pluto and hide at the edge of the system where the remnants dare not go.

Read the sparse, half-finished, and unhinged descriptions, sourced from real papers, physical and orbital data, and whatever answers when you contemplate what to write as flavor text for 2012 VP113.

Rejoice in the custom orbital calculations that allow the accurate modeling of eccentricity, even if the many eccentric objects at the edge of the solar system appear nearly stationary and are subjected to such a steep logarithm that their orbits are practically circular.

Much of the system is customizable. So if you want to disable the annoying remnants, disable pirate and pather markets, or enable some obscure set of minor planets, you can do that.

Gallery

Earth, Luna, Kamo'oalewa, and assorted entities

Mercury and imminent death

Venus and ordos

Mars, Phobos, Deimos, and ordos

Jupiter, Ganymede, Callisto, Io, Amalthea, Thebe, and Metis

Saturn, Rhea, Dione, Tethys, Enceladus, Mimas, Janus, Epimetheus, Prometheus, Pandora, Helene, Atlas, Telesto, Kiviuq, and Methone

Uranus, Ariel, Miranda, Puck (Luddic Path), Portia, Cressida, Belinda, Rosalind, Desdemona, and Cordelia

Neptune (TRUECOLOR, DON'T BELIEVE THE LIES), Triton, Proteus, Nereid, Larissa, Galatea, Despina, Thalassa, and Naiad.

Pluto-Charon, Hydra, Nix, Kerberos

Ceres, Vesta, and the Asteroid Belt – split into the Inner, Middle, Outer belts. With the Cybele and Hungarian groups additionally added.

Math trigger warning

The Planets and confirmed Dwarf Planets modeled on Desmos.

Compatability and issues
Integrations:
Terraforming and Station Construction - several stations exist, and the colonization is balanced with the intention that you have TASC or another terraforming mod.
Industrial Evolution - adds artillery, stations, and industrial ruins conditions. NOTE: Placing the Industrial Evolution relays on Sol's many planets is not recommended for performance reasons.
Ashes of The Domain - adds Pre-Collapse Facilities to several minor planets. - has config setting to force colony names to the name of planet (by default disabled)
Random Assortment of Things - adds some conditions around the place.
Unkown Skies - adds some conditions around the place.
Wide Horizons - now fully compatable.
Version Checker - functional.
TriOs - Semi-compatable.

Performance note:
Industrial Evolution - Military/Interstellar Relays and Rougue object events can cause lag

Known issues:
I'm going to post known issues here, and their status for next patch
None major
Ashes of The Domain: system viewer doesnt show full system, since I use a custom system size.

FAQs
Q: What's the difference between this and the other Solar System mod?
A: I'm a big nerd and I wanted to play with more than 12 world, and given the effort that goes into mapping the system, I'ts a shame to rely on random generation. I don't, every asteroid (bar 10 for gameplay reasons) is a real asteroid at a real location on the starmap based on where it would be in ~8,000 years. New Orbit types were created just to simulate the keplerian motion of eccentric bodies as they zip closer and further from their parents, all to create a fun and educational experience.

Everybody can name the 9 10 8 ?9? planets, but can you name the 7-> like 30? Dwarf planets?
Chiron, in my classics class? I mean the centaur is pretty cool, but come on, this is greek, not cometary geology.

Solsector is pretty unstable though :|
